title: Partitime — React × Contract × Vanilla JS × four backends
description: A controlled Partiful-style experiment: one deterministic event/RSVP/wall product contract is implemented as an explicit 3×4 matrix across React, Contract, and framework-free browser JavaScript, backed by Snapback, Supabase, Convex, and plain SQLite.

backend.source: snapback/schema.mjs + snapback/functions.mjs + snapback/handlers.mjs; comparison providers under backends/
backend.stalenessPolicy: committed; regenerate with codegen; freshness tracked by artifacts.json inputsHash

headless.toolchain: bun, cargo, local Supabase and Convex credentials

react-supabase-realtime.toolchain: bun, Vite, Chrome, @supabase/supabase-js, hosted Supabase Realtime

react-convex-realtime.toolchain: bun, Vite, Chrome, convex/browser, hosted Convex WebSocket

react-expo-android-online.toolchain: Expo, React Native, Android SDK/emulator, Gradle, Snapback server

react-expo-ios-online.toolchain: Expo, React Native, Xcode/iOS Simulator, Snapback server

headless: all four providers expose the same deterministic event projection and ordering
RSVP is idempotent per event/person on every provider
create event, atomic host seat, and wall post complete on every provider; temporary remote rows are scoped and removed
event, RSVP, and wall rows have portable normalized shapes
browserMatrix: all twelve independently built cells boot and identify their arm/backend
the shared feed and event detail render from each real provider
an RSVP mutation becomes observable in the selected cell
the vanilla row replaces feed/detail subscription scopes without leaking handles
vanillaLifecycle: late handle resolution and stale observer delivery are fenced
page close is terminal and idempotently disposes the current scope
frameworkNeutralClient: same-key external-store siblings share one upstream attempt and dispose independently
the original vanilla lifecycle suite passes against shipped ExternalQueryScope
the full client root and lifecycle primitive execute through direct browser ESM without transforms
all four vanilla cells expose ordered startup milestones after the lifecycle replacement
reactClient: React Strict Mode replay, same-key sharing, different-key isolation, A-to-B-to-A replacement, and unmount disposal pass
Partitime React web consumes @expo/snapback-react and the same generated provider operations
providerNativeReactFollowup: React uses each provider's browser-native client without the comparison gateway
an isolated acceptance event receives out-of-band updates through the measured push transport with no polling fallback
normal React root teardown disposes query scopes and closes the provider client
reactExpoAndroidOnline: generated-function initial data and optimistic authoritative settlement
authority rotation, background/foreground, offline rows, and authoritative reconnect
release carrier excludes Snapback server code and claims Online only
reactExpoIosOnline: generated-function initial data and optimistic authoritative settlement
authority rotation, background/foreground, offline rows, and authoritative reconnect
release carrier excludes Snapback server code and claims Online only

capabilityGaps: the original build misread a secret-only OpenAPI-root 401 as a rejected publishable key, so the frozen Supabase web cells use a local Bun gateway and server-only Postgres credentials; the corrected probe and the browser-direct supabase-realtime follow-up cell landed 2026-07-20

the frozen portable comparison providers poll every second; separate React follow-up cells exercise browser-direct Supabase Realtime and Convex WebSocket push, while Contract-generated direct bindings remain open
the comparison builds still use Vite even though a separate direct-ESM compatibility receipt passes
React Expo Android and iOS Online each pass their clean cumulative per-OS profiles
Exact Native iOS and Android Parity profiles remain pending
hosted deployment and production authentication are outside this local comparison

capabilityGapsBoundary.reason: These entries describe frozen matrix cells and comparison limits, not current platform GAP rows.

notClaiming: production auth, row-level security, or tenant isolation (personas are trusted local demo identities)

equal realtime transports in the frozen matrix: polling is labeled in the Supabase, Convex, and SQLite cells; the two React-only direct follow-ups are partial evidence, not a completed cross-authoring matrix
benchmark-quality performance results or backend pricing comparisons
twelve separately maintained UI codebases: each authoring row intentionally shares source across its four backend builds
React Expo Parity or local-first execution: the current native JavaScript carrier is Online only
